text:
sam: Quick observation: over the last 48h a few GPU nodegroups have a bunch of mostly-empty nodes that never get scaled down. PDBs + local scratch + a conservative CA config seem to be the combo. Thinking we should try a small CA flag tweak and a graceful drain window for GPUs.

maria: Do you have concrete flags in mind? we need to be careful with preemptible/spot pools and racing deletes.

sam: Draft proposal: change autoscaler deployment args to pack GPUs better and be more aggressive about empty nodes while still safe for PDBs. Example args: 

```yaml
- --expander=least-waste
- --scale-down-enabled=true
- --scale-down-unneeded-time=7m
- --scale-down-unready-time=8m
- --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45
- --balance-similar-node-groups=true
- --max-empty-bulk-delete=6
```

The idea: least-waste + lower unneeded-time should let CA consolidate GPU workloads into fewer nodes faster. 0.45 util threshold avoids tiny-headroom nodes.

lee: Two quick notes: 1) pods with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"` will block scale-down — we have ~12 ML-kit pods with that annotation. 2) PDBs still block eviction even if safe-to-evict is true. I pulled a CA log snippet earlier: 

```
I0714 14:02:21.123456 1 scale_down.go:467] Node gpu-node-7 is unneeded for 25m0s, removing it would violate PodDisruptionBudget for deployment/model-service: desired: 2, minAvailable: 2
I0714 14:02:21.123458 1 scale_down.go:512] Skipping scale down: node has local storage
```

lee: So we need to address both annotations and local storage bites. For local scratch we can run a small sidecar to flush temp storage to S3 or convert scratch to ephemeral that CA will ignore.

omar: For spot/preemptible pools I recommend *not* increasing bulk delete too high. For dedicated GPU nodegroups (non-spot) pushing max-empty-bulk-delete=6 is fine; for spot pools keep it at 2. We should have separate autoscaler configs per nodegroup class if possible.

maria: Could we instead do a staged rollout: change expander + util threshold in canary cluster first, then lower unneeded-time for 24h canary, then bulk-delete bump? safer.

sam: Agreed. Plan: 
1) Add an annotation to non-evictable pods we control to flip safe-to-evict to true when they can be drained. (CI/job-runner/long-runner owners notified)
2) Canary autoscaler change in `gpu-canary` nodepool: expander=least-waste, util=0.45, unneeded-time=7m, max-empty-bulk-delete=3
3) Monitor grafana: gpu.node.count, autoscaler.scaleDownCandidates, pod.evictions, PDB-blocks for 12h
4) If green, roll to dedicated pools and leave spot pools with conservative bulk-delete=2

devops-bot: PR opened: https://git.internal/repo/infra/cluster-autoscaler/PR-421 (canary only). Will add rollout plan and Grafana dashboards to the PR description. :shipit:

lee: +1 on canary. Also add a small hook to run `kubectl get pdb -A` before/after to ensure no unexpected PDB violations. I can add that to the deploy job.

omar: One more: create a `priorityClass` for batch-gpu-short jobs with lower priority so CA+kube-scheduler can preempt them in edge cases and free nodes for inference. Tiny YAML: 

```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: batch-gpu-low
value: -100
globalDefault: false
description: "Lower priority for opportunistic GPU batch jobs"
```

sam: Good call. I'll coordinate owners to flip annotations and we can kick off the canary this afternoon. If anyone sees unexpected eviction noise after the first 30m ping here.

maria: I'll watch the dashboards and PDB checks. ping me when PR merges.

sam: thanks — will post the rollout link once the canary deploy job launches.
